newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors demand 11 years for Krenz.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors demand 11 years for Krenz.

text.p: State prosecutors on Thursday demanded an 11-year jail sentence for Egon Krenz, East Germany's last hardline communist leader, blaming him for the Cold War killings of citizens trying to flee to the West.

Prosecutor Bernhard Jahntz said Krenz, who succeeded Erich Honecker as party chief when the East German state began to crumble in 1989, bore direct responsibility for the killings as a long-time member of the ruling Politburo executive body.

"The murderous border regime was created by people like Erich Honecker and perpetuated by people like Egon Krenz," Jahntz told the Berlin court trying the former leader and two other top East German officials on manslaughter charges.
Jahntz also demanded nine years' jail for East Berlin communist party chief Guenter Schabowski and seven and a half years for economic policy supremo Guenther Kleiber.
Krenz has denied responsibility for the killings at the Berlin Wall and the fortified border which divided the two Germanys, saying they were simply a product of the Cold War.
Krenz, who was long seen as a Honecker's protege, has accused prosecutors of conducting a politically-motivated trial and slammed them for pursuing "victor's justice".

The marathon trial has dragged on for more than one and a half years. In a bid to speed up the process, prosecutors have dropped many of the charges they originally levelled against the three former Politburo members.
They are now all charged with the manslaughter of three refugees while Krenz alone is also charged in a fourth case.
